#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Fix propagating optional CRI runtime conditions.

This is needed because the CRI API states that optional runtime conditions will be "exposed to users to help them understand the status of the system", but the conditions were not visible via the core API.

https://github.com/kubernetes/cri-api/blob/v0.29.1/pkg/apis/runtime/v1/api.proto#L1496-L1518

```protobuf
// RuntimeCondition contains condition information for the runtime.
// There are 2 kinds of runtime conditions:
// 1. Required conditions: Conditions are required for kubelet to work
// properly. If any required condition is unmet, the node will be not ready.
// The required conditions include:
//   * RuntimeReady: RuntimeReady means the runtime is up and ready to accept
//   basic containers e.g. container only needs host network.
//   * NetworkReady: NetworkReady means the runtime network is up and ready to
//   accept containers which require container network.
// 2. Optional conditions: Conditions are informative to the user, but kubelet
// will not rely on. Since condition type is an arbitrary string, all conditions
// not required are optional. These conditions will be exposed to users to help
// them understand the status of the system.
message RuntimeCondition {
    // Type of runtime condition.
    string type = 1;
    // Status of the condition, one of true/false. Default: false.
    bool status = 2;
    // Brief CamelCase string containing reason for the condition's last transition.
    string reason = 3;
    // Human-readable message indicating details about last transition.
    string message = 4;
}
```

```console
$ kubectl get nodes -o json | jq .items[0].status.conditions
[
  {
    "lastHeartbeatTime": "2024-02-07T10:01:49Z",
    "lastTransitionTime": "2024-02-07T04:19:34Z",
    "message": "kubelet has sufficient memory available",
    "reason": "KubeletHasSufficientMemory",
    "status": "False",
    "type": "MemoryPressure"
  },
  {
    "lastHeartbeatTime": "2024-02-07T10:01:49Z",
    "lastTransitionTime": "2024-02-07T04:19:34Z",
    "message": "kubelet has no disk pressure",
    "reason": "KubeletHasNoDiskPressure",
    "status": "False",
    "type": "DiskPressure"
  },
  {
    "lastHeartbeatTime": "2024-02-07T10:01:49Z",
    "lastTransitionTime": "2024-02-07T04:19:34Z",
    "message": "kubelet has sufficient PID available",
    "reason": "KubeletHasSufficientPID",
    "status": "False",
    "type": "PIDPressure"
  },
  {
    "lastHeartbeatTime": "2024-02-07T10:01:49Z",
    "lastTransitionTime": "2024-02-07T04:19:56Z",
    "message": "kubelet is posting ready status",
    "reason": "KubeletReady",
    "status": "True",
    "type": "Ready"
  },
  {
    "lastHeartbeatTime": "2024-02-07T10:01:49Z",
    "lastTransitionTime": "2024-02-07T10:01:49Z",
    "message": "{\"io.containerd.deprecation/pull-schema-1-image\":\"Schema 1 images are deprecated since containerd v1.7 and removed in containerd v2.0. Since containerd v1.7.8, schema 1 images are identified by the \\\"io.containerd.image/converted-docker-schema1\\\" label.\"}",
    "reason": "ContainerdHasDeprecationWarnings",
    "status": "False",
    "type": "ContainerdHasNoDeprecationWarnings"
  }
]
```

`ContainerdHasNoDeprecationWarning` is proposed in:
- https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/9767

The condition is set to "True" if no deprecated feature is being used.

@aojea

my reasons why I don't think this is a good idea:
- isolation domains, node.status is a subresource that has rbac controls, this will make that a component that is not the kubelet can impersonate the kubelet to add arbitrary conditions
- scalability issues, as there is no control on this conditions container runtimes may be spamming the conditions on the status and generating instability on the cluster, as each modification of the node object will trigger a reconcilation on the nodes watching the node
- not clear that this solves the problem statement, as this is supposed to inform that something is causing problems with the container runtime, but  the runtime already has a condition to indicate that, so this seems to intent to be used only  for warning conditions, and here there is a fine line on what can be considerable appropriate by one or other vendor to expose to the users , and all these vendors will have zero control over this, since will be a pure controller runtime decision what conditions will be published

issue_context.title: kubelet ignores optional CRI runtime conditions (kubelet will not rely on them, but it should somehow make them visible via kubectl)
comments: /sig node

> Out of curiosity, I do not see any requirement that the type has to be a positive phrase. 

True, but I guess it is implied.

containerd will expose `ContainerdHasNoDeprecationWarning` conditions like this
```json
{                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        
  "status": {                
    "conditions": [         
      {                             
        "type": "RuntimeReady",   
        "status": true,          
        "reason": "",                 
        "message": ""                        
      },                                
      {                  
        "type": "NetworkReady",
        "status": true,                                                                                                             
        "reason": "",             
        "message": "" 
      },                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
      {
        "type": "ContainerdHasNoDeprecationWarning",
        "status": false,
        "reason": "[\"io.containerd.deprecation/pull-schema-1-image\"]",
        "message": "{\"io.containerd.deprecation/pull-schema-1-image\":\"Schema 1 images are deprecated since containerd v1.7 and removed in containerd v2.0. Since containerd v1.7.8, schema 1 images are identified by the \\\"io.containerd.image/converted-docker-schema1\\\" label.\"}"
      }                    
    ]                      
  }, 
...
}
```

The condition is set to true when there is no warning about deprecated features being used.

- https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/9767

I don't know if is a great UX to submit an arbitrary number of conditions to the Node object, as it can create confusion since there is no standardization on those, so containerd, kata, ... and crio clusters will provide different conditions

> I don't know if is a great UX to submit an arbitrary number of conditions to the Node object, as it can create confusion since there is no standardization on those, so containerd, kata, ... and crio clusters will provide different conditions

Still better than watching entire daemon logs though.

PR:
- https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123155

> Still better than watching entire daemon logs though.

but can you explain what kind of conditions are expected here for those of us that are not familiar with the container runtime conditions?

Node conditions are meant to be representing the node status https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/node/node-status/#condition , and conditions can taint the node https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/taint-and-toleration/#taint-nodes-by-condition , if the runtime is not ready already has a condition to declare that in the node `RuntimeReady` 

Also, other components running in the node and interfacing with the kubelet may ask for the same demand ...
@AkihiroSuda  You beat me to it with that PR :)

@aojea 

> but can you explain what kind of conditions are expected here for those of us that are not familiar with the container runtime conditions?

This will be used for propagating warning when a deprecated containerd feature (such as pulling Schema1 images) is used.
Technologically, users could just read the daemon log or use `ctr deprecations list` to inspect the warnings,
but it is often hard and there is a request to expose them as node statuses.

https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/9765#issuecomment-1928769556

> Node conditions are meant to be representing the node status https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/node/node-status/#condition , and conditions can taint the node https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/scheduling-eviction/taint-and-toleration/#taint-nodes-by-condition , if the runtime is not ready already has a condition to declare that in the node RuntimeReady

As stated in https://github.com/kubernetes/cri-api/blob/v0.29.1/pkg/apis/runtime/v1/api.proto#L1496-L1518 , 
`kubelet will not rely on` these `Optional conditions`.
This condition does not affect `RuntimeReady`, and does not affect taints.

> Also, other components running in the node and interfacing with the kubelet may ask for the same demand ...

Other components should have been already aware that `k get nodes` may print "strange" conditions.

https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/api/core/v1#NodeConditionType

```
A cloud provider may set a condition not listed here.
```

Specifically for the deprecation messages, this may confuse some customers. In GKE, for example, we set mirrors using "old way" because there are customers who are adding other mirrors this way. So we have a separate detection mechanism that will tell those customers that the change is needed and we will switch the config mode when we are sure that it will not break those customers customizing things manually.

If this will be exposed widely, we may need to have some mechanism to hide certain deprecation warnings than.

CC: @yujuhong
cc @thockin

> If this will be exposed widely, we may need to have some mechanism to hide certain deprecation warnings than.

For containerd, we may have an allow list or a deny list to filter deprecation IDs
https://github.com/containerd/containerd/pull/9767#discussion_r1480247726

IIRC, the intention of having these optional condition message was to surface them to the users through some mechanism upon inspection (for example, `crictl info`). It was never proposed to directly include them to the node conditions.

> Other components should have been already aware that `k get nodes` may print "strange" conditions.

My understanding is that the cloud provider and other components are given the capability to patch the nodes, but in this case, kubelet simply passes whatever the runtime provides to the node status.

> IIRC, the intention of having these optional condition message was to surface them to the users through some mechanism upon inspection (for example, crictl info). It was never proposed to directly include them to the node conditions.

How can the user inspect them via `kubectl get` ?
I don't think that users should have to ssh into nodes to run crictl.

ok, so the problem here is how to expose to the users container runtime deprecation information

I personally don't think that using the node.status.condition as a logging service for runtimes is the best option, it also gives the temptation to runtimes to start abusing this mechanism and there is not control in the kubelet for that, as this can mean 2 or 1000 conditions ...

I assume that this will also cluster-wide as I don´t expect mixed versions of runtimes on the cluster, why not sending an Event instead at startup? the kubelet can send an event with this information of the runtime

> there is not control in the kubelet for that, as this can mean 2 or 1000 conditions ...
>
> I assume that this will also cluster-wide as I don´t expect mixed versions of runtimes on the cluster, why not sending an Event instead at startup? the kubelet can send an event with this information of the runtime

Users may still see 1000 events, no?
/triage accepted
/kind feature

> > there is not control in the kubelet for that, as this can mean 2 or 1000 conditions ...
> > I assume that this will also cluster-wide as I don´t expect mixed versions of runtimes on the cluster, why not sending an Event instead at startup? the kubelet can send an event with this information of the runtime
> 
> Users may still see 1000 events, no?

Events are de-duplicated, and often have separate storage handling. IMO this is a good use case for Warning events, which I think are under-utilized. Events aren't included with `kubectl get node`, but should be included with `kubectl describe node`.
